title: The --json result documents
summary: With --json every command writes exactly one JSON document, on one line, to standard output.

items.text: The version of the document layout, {{schemaVersion}}. It changes only when a document changes incompatibly; adding a key is not a change, so ignore keys and operations you do not know.
true for a result, false for a failure.
The canonical name of the command that ran (null in a failure when no command was selected).
The document is deterministic: fixed key order, invariant-culture numbers, one line, ASCII only (other characters are written as \uXXXX). Standard error is not part of it.

sections.title: Fields of render, convert, and the verbs

items.text: {name, version} of the tool.

{path, format, natural: {width, height}}, and for a document pageCount and page; and fragment, the text after the # of an input path such as part.scad#def.width=20 (path is then the file; the member is absent for an input without a fragment). The same member is in the a and b of compare and in each cell of montage.

Every step that was applied, in order; each has an op key (render, embed, auto-orient, resize, fit, flatten, crop, rotate, flip, pad, and the photo operations) and its own fields. With --all-pages every operation also carries its page. The verbs are crop, resize, rotate, flip, and pad.
One entry per file written: {path, format, width, height, bytes} and page for a document.
The features that were left out of the picture; see the diagnostics section below.
The text an OpenSCAD model printed with echo.

Only for an OpenSCAD model: the points it declared with echo("anchor", "name", [x, y, z]), in echo order, each {name, point: [x, y, z], pixel: [x, y] or null, inside}. pixel is the position in the written picture, from its top-left corner, after the pixel steps; see 'canvasnet help scad'.

input {path, format, bytes} and one of image, document {pageCount, pages[]}, model {modules, functions, directives}, chart, or diagram (chart and diagram follow an image object with the laid-out size).

For a Mermaid diagram (info): {type, supported, direction, title, accTitle, nodes, edges, subgraphs}. type is the diagram type (flowchart for flowchart and graph, sequence for sequenceDiagram); supported is false for a type this version does not draw yet (class, state, and so on), which renders as an empty picture with the diagnostic mermaid-diagram-unsupported; for a sequence diagram, nodes, edges, and subgraphs count the participants, the messages, and the boxes; direction, title, and accTitle are present when the diagram has them.

tool, library, inputs[], outputs[], quality {min, max, default}, and maxDimension. Each inputs[] entry has format, kind, extensions, multiPage, vector, and helpTopic: the topic of 'canvasnet help <topic>' that describes the format (raster for png, jpeg, bmp, tiff, gif, and jpeg2000).
Described in their own help: run 'canvasnet help compare', 'canvasnet help montage', or 'canvasnet help inspect'.
kind is index, command, topic, examples, or example; see the help section below.
Where the report comes from: scad, vega-lite, mermaid, pptx, vsdx, or svg. PDF and raster images have no diagnostics channel.
unsupported for a feature that was left out, or warning for a questionable construct that still rendered.

The stable generic identifier of the report, for example scad-module-surface, vl-mark-geoshape, svg-image-unresolved, or image-page-out-of-range. A warning of a SCAD model always has the code scad-warning, a warning of a Vega-Lite chart the code vega-lite-warning, and a warning of a Mermaid diagram the code mermaid-warning; the finer identifier is in detail.
A description; for a model, chart, or diagram it gives file, line, and column.

Only when the code is generic: the finer identifier of the library, for example scad-anchor-invalid for a scad-warning, vl-unknown-property for a vega-lite-warning, or mermaid-config-unknown-key for a mermaid-warning. Branch on code and detail, never on the message.

Only when the file gave a position: {file, line, column} for a model or a diagram, or {file, pointer, line, column} for a chart (the JSON pointer of the offending property); a member that is not known is left out.

Only for a report about an embedded file (an SVG that links other files): the files, outermost first, that lead to it, as folder-relative names (a link that was not drawn names the SVG file that contains it). The message starts with the href as written.
The page of a document the report belongs to.

Without --json the same reports are written to standard error as 'Unsupported: <code>: <message>' or 'Warning: <code>: <message>' lines (and echo as 'ECHO: <text>'); with --json standard error carries none of them, so standard output stays one JSON document.

{code, message, hint}: code is one of the stable codes of the errors topic ('canvasnet help errors'); hint is omitted when there is none. The document has no exit-code field: the exit code of every failure is 1.
A failure document is written only when --json is given and --silent is not. A failed compare gate also carries the fields of the comparison.
topic is topics; usage, commands[], topics[] ({name, aliases, summary}), and globalOptions[].
topic is the command name; aliases, summary, usage, options[], and globalOptions[]. An option is {name, aliases, takesValue, valueName, description}.
topic, aliases, title, summary, sections[] ({id, title, items[] of {term, text}}), and examples[] ({name, kind, language, fileName, description, content}).
topic and examples[] without the content, for 'canvasnet help <topic> --examples --json'.
topic and one example object, for 'canvasnet help <topic> --example <name> --json'.
